title: Victor Shoup
name: Victor Shoup
summary: Cryptographer and NYU professor known for research on cryptographic protocols and number-theoretic algorithms, and for the NTL software library.
whyThisMatters: Victor Shoup is included for documented contributions to the technical and formal foundations of computer security and cryptography.

sections.overview:
Victor Shoup is a professor at NYU Courant whose research covers cryptography, computational number theory, and algorithms. He also created NTL, a widely used open-source C++ library for number-theory computations.

Security relevance

Public-key cryptography depends heavily on reliable arithmetic over large integers and finite fields. Shoup’s research and software made these mathematical foundations more accessible to researchers and implementers.

timeline.event: Receives a Ph.D. in computer science from the University of Wisconsin–Madison.
Develops NTL, a number-theory library used in cryptographic research and implementation.
Publishes a graduate course text on applied cryptography.
Serves as editor for ISO 18033-2 on public-key encryption.
